description: How much credit support will NVIDIA have extended to AI cloud partners for their financing or capacity commitments, as disclosed in its filings, by the check date?
outcome: The amount and form of credit support, guarantees or similar obligations NVIDIA discloses for AI cloud partners.
period: By 2027-12-31, a check date within 18 months of the item, using NVIDIA's annual report and quarterly filings.

description: Will NVIDIA's Vera Rubin next-generation AI chip platform begin shipping by the end of calendar 2026?
outcome: First shipments of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin AI chip platform.
period: By 2026-12-31 (calendar year-end; the item says Vera Rubin is in full production and 'could begin shipping later this year').

description: Will the Chinese government permit Nvidia to sell its H200 AI chips in China, allowing Nvidia to resume China data-center chip sales, by the check date?
outcome: A decision by China's government to allow — or continue blocking — Nvidia H200 AI-chip sales in China.
period: By Nvidia's fiscal year-end in late January 2027 (the current fiscal year-end fixed by the item's July 2026 date, per the pending-regulatory-decision default).

description: Will the four largest AI hyperscalers' combined data-center capital expenditures reach roughly $1 trillion in calendar 2027, up from about $650 billion planned for calendar 2026?
outcome: The four largest AI hyperscalers' combined calendar-2027 data-center capital expenditures, versus the ~$650 billion planned for calendar 2026.
period: Calendar 2027; check after the four hyperscalers report Q4 2027 results (early 2028), the release date of the aggregate annual capex figures.

description: Will Nvidia's Kyber rack-scale architecture, the rack system designed to house its Vera Rubin Ultra chips, begin shipping by the end of calendar 2028, after SemiAnalysis reported a delay of more than 12 months to 2028?
outcome: First shipments of Nvidia's Kyber rack-scale architecture / Vera Rubin Ultra systems.
period: By 2028-12-31 (SemiAnalysis reports the Kyber/Rubin Ultra debut pushed from 2027 to 2028).

description: How large will NVIDIA's supply purchase commitments be at its next annual report, and how much of that obligation is tied to AI capacity that must be absorbed?
outcome: NVIDIA's total purchase and supply commitments disclosed in its annual report (and updated in 10-Qs).
period: At NVIDIA's next annual report (fiscal-2027 Form 10-K, expected around February 2027; the obligation is already undertaken, so it is tracked by its amount at the next annual report).

description: Will Chinese enterprises shift roughly 46% of their AI-accelerator budgets to domestic suppliers within the next 12 months, up from about 30% today, reducing demand for Nvidia-class imported accelerators?
outcome: The share of Chinese AI-accelerator budgets allocated to domestic suppliers within 12 months, versus roughly 30% today.
period: By 2027-07-07, within 12 months of the July 2026 item (the next calendar year); settled by the next industry survey release.

description: Will DRAM and NAND memory-chip contract prices at the end of calendar 2027 be higher than at the end of calendar 2026 — i.e., will the memory shortage Micron says could last until 2028 keep prices elevated through next year?
outcome: End-2027 DRAM/NAND contract price levels versus end-2026, and whether memory supply remains tight through calendar 2027.
period: Calendar 2027; checked against Q4 2027 memory contract-price assessments published in early 2028 (release date of the aggregate price the thesis tracks).

description: How much credit support (guarantees or credit enhancement for AI cloud partners' infrastructure financing) will NVIDIA have extended under its revenue-sharing and credit-support model by its next annual report?
outcome: The disclosed amount of credit support or guarantee exposure NVIDIA has committed to AI cloud partners under the new revenue-sharing and credit-support model.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K, fiscal year ending late January 2027); set as the reporting date for an obligation being undertaken, per section 3.

description: Will NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin AI chip platform, the product line that carries its data center value, reach first customer shipments by the end of 2026?
outcome: First shipments of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform occurring by end-2026, as the item says shipments 'could begin later this year'.
period: 2026 year-end; set from the item's statement that Vera Rubin could begin shipping 'later this year' (2026), checked against NVIDIA's quarterly results and shipment/availability confirmations during the year.

description: Will Beijing permit imports/sales of Nvidia's H200 AI chips into China by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end?
outcome: A Chinese government decision (or continuation of the ban) on allowing Nvidia H200 AI-chip sales into China.
period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (fiscal year ending late January 2027); the item gives no date for China's decision, so this pending regulatory decision is checked at the current fiscal year-end, per section 3.

description: Will the four largest AI hyperscalers' combined data center capital expenditures reach roughly $1 trillion in calendar 2027, up from about $650 billion planned for 2026, as NVIDIA projects?
outcome: The combined 2027 data center capital expenditures of the four largest AI hyperscalers, measured against NVIDIA's projection that the figure could reach $1 trillion.
period: Calendar 2027; confirmed when the four hyperscalers report full-year 2027 capital expenditures in their Q4-2027/annual filings (early 2028). Set from the item's 'next year ... $1 trillion' projection.

description: Will Nvidia's Kyber rack-scale architecture for Vera Rubin Ultra (the NVL144 rack system housing its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips) reach first customer shipments in 2027 as originally planned, or slip to 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: Timing of first customer shipments of Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack system for Vera Rubin Ultra — 2027 (as originally slated) versus 2028 (as SemiAnalysis reports).
period: 2027–2028; the item reports the debut slipped from 2027 to 2028, checked against Nvidia's shipment/availability confirmations in its quarterly results and product disclosures.

description: How large will NVIDIA's supply purchase commitments (obligations to buy memory, components and capacity) be at its next annual report, after the company was reported to carry $119 billion of supply commitments?
outcome: The dollar amount of NVIDIA's supply purchase commitments disclosed in its FY2027 Form 10-K, measured against the $119 billion the item reports.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K, fiscal year ending late January 2027); set as the reporting date for an obligation already undertaken, per section 3.

description: Will Nvidia's Rubin Ultra GPUs — now a dual-chiplet part after the reported switch from a quad-chiplet design — reach first customer shipments in calendar 2027 as the item indicates they are slated to?
outcome: First customer shipments of Nvidia's Rubin Ultra GPUs occurring in 2027, whether in Oberon racks while the Kyber rack slips to 2028 or in Kyber.
period: Calendar 2027; set from the item's references to "2027's Rubin Ultra GPUs" and to the Kyber rack (reported delayed to 2028) as the cabinet "meant for" them, checked against Nvidia's quarterly results and product availability/shipment confirmations during 2027.

description: Will the U.S. Congress enact legislation to phase out Chinese-made lidar sensors — including Hesai's, which the item says is one option automakers can integrate into Nvidia's DRIVE Hyperion autonomous-vehicle platform — in the United States by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end?
outcome: Enactment (or failure) of U.S. legislation phasing out Chinese-made lidar (e.g., Hesai's) from U.S. autonomous systems, which would remove a low-cost lidar option from Nvidia's autonomous-vehicle platform.
period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (fiscal year ending late January 2027); the item gives no date for the proposed legislation, so per section 3 the pending regulatory decision is checked at the current fiscal year-end.

description: Will Chinese firms shift 46% of their AI-accelerator budgets to domestic suppliers within 12 months (by mid-2027), up from roughly 30% today, reducing Nvidia's addressable China accelerator demand?
outcome: The share of Chinese firms' AI-accelerator budgets allocated to domestic suppliers, measured against the survey's 46% target within 12 months.
period: Within 12 months of the July 2026 item (by mid-2027); set from the survey's 'within 12 months' horizon, checked against the next industry survey and Nvidia's China revenue disclosures.

description: Will the U.S. Commerce Department's inquiry into whether Chinese AI firm DeepSeek obtained restricted Nvidia chips through Singapore/Malaysia intermediaries result in a public enforcement action or new export restriction affecting Nvidia's China business (e.g., findings, entity-list designations, or tighter transshipment controls) by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end?
outcome: A public U.S. Commerce Department/BIS finding, enforcement action, or new export restriction stemming from the DeepSeek/diversion-of-Nvidia-chips inquiry, versus no such action.
period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (fiscal year ending late January 2027); the item gives no date for the Commerce inquiry's conclusion, so this pending regulatory matter is checked at the current fiscal year-end, per section 3.

description: How much credit support will NVIDIA have extended to AI cloud partners under the revenue-sharing and credit-support model it is introducing, as disclosed in its guarantee and commitment disclosures?
outcome: The amount of credit support / backstop exposure NVIDIA has extended to AI cloud partners' infrastructure financing, as reported in NVIDIA's filings.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report — FY2027 Form 10-K for the fiscal year ending late January 2027, expected filed around February 2027 (set by the reason: an obligation already undertaken is tracked by its amount at the next annual report).

description: Will NVIDIA's Vera Rubin next-generation AI chip platform begin shipping to customers by the end of calendar 2026?
outcome: First shipments (initial customer deliveries / revenue recognition) of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform, the next-generation GPU line carrying the company's data-center value.
period: Calendar 2026 — the item says Vera Rubin is 'in full production and could begin shipping later this year'; outcome checked at NVIDIA's fourth-quarter FY2027 report (fiscal year ending late January 2027, expected ~February 2027) that would confirm shipments in calendar 2026.

description: Will the Chinese government allow Nvidia to sell its H200 (and other U.S.-approved) AI chips to Chinese commercial customers, re-opening Nvidia's China data-center revenue, or will it continue to bar Nvidia from the China market?
outcome: Whether China permits Nvidia to sell H200/approved AI chips to Chinese customers (resumption of Nvidia China revenue), versus continued exclusion of Nvidia despite the U.S. having cleared H200 exports.
period: NVIDIA FY2027, fiscal year ending late January 2027 (set by the reason: a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end); checked at NVIDIA's Q4 FY2027 report (~February 2027) and any Chinese regulatory announcement.

description: How much will the big four AI hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta) spend in combined data center capital expenditures in calendar 2026 and 2027 — the aggregate demand pool that NVIDIA's data-center revenue depends on?
outcome: The big four AI hyperscalers' combined data center capital expenditure for calendar 2026 (and NVIDIA's projected 2027 level), as disclosed in their earnings and capex guidance.
period: Calendar 2026, checked against the big four hyperscalers' quarterly capex disclosures and full-year figures through their Q4 2026 reports (early 2027); the 2027 level is checked through their 2027 quarterly reports. Set from the item's 'this year'/'next year' framing relative to its 2026-07-04 publication date.

description: Will Nvidia's Kyber rack-scale architecture — the rack system designed to house its Rubin Ultra chips — reach first customer shipments in 2028, rather than 2027 as previously slated or later still, and will the NVL576 eight-rack scale-up system follow it into volume?
outcome: First customer shipments / volume availability of the Kyber NVL144 rack (144 GPUs per cabinet) and of the NVL576 eight-rack optical scale-up system that SemiAnalysis says has slipped from 2027 to 2028 on PCB-midplane manufacturability problems.
period: Calendar 2028 — the debut date the item reports (delayed more than 12 months from the 2027 Vera Rubin Ultra launch); checked against Nvidia's shipment and product disclosures through its FY2029 Form 10-K (fiscal year ending late January 2029).

description: How large will NVIDIA's supply purchase commitments be at its next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K) — i.e., how much committed purchase volume is the company carrying into the memory and CoWoS/component supply chain, and how much of it is take-or-pay?
outcome: The dollar amount of NVIDIA's purchase/supply commitments disclosed in the contractual obligations and purchase commitments disclosures of its FY2027 Form 10-K, compared with the $119 billion cited in this item.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report — FY2027 Form 10-K for the fiscal year ending late January 2027, expected filed around February 2027 (set by the reason: an obligation already undertaken is tracked by its amount at the next annual report).

description: How large will the custom AI ASIC (hyperscaler XPU) pool be in calendar 2027 — specifically, what will Broadcom's and Marvell's combined AI custom-silicon revenue be, and how fast is it growing relative to NVIDIA's GPU accelerator revenue?
outcome: Broadcom's and Marvell's combined AI semiconductor/custom silicon revenue for calendar 2027, as disclosed in their quarterly reports, versus the growth of NVIDIA's data-center accelerator revenue.
period: Calendar 2027 — checked against Broadcom's and Marvell's quarterly AI semiconductor revenue disclosures through their reports covering calendar 2027 (reported through early 2028). Set as next calendar year relative to the item's 2026-07-06 publication.

description: What will memory (HBM/DRAM) contract prices be in calendar 2027 — i.e., how much will memory input costs inflate the bill of materials for NVIDIA's AI systems and pressure its gross margin or supply availability?
outcome: The level and direction of HBM/DRAM contract prices in calendar 2027 as reported by price trackers and by the memory makers' (Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung) quarterly pricing, margin and capacity disclosures.
period: Calendar 2027, checked against quarterly memory contract price releases and the memory makers' quarterly results through calendar 2027. Set as next calendar year relative to the item's 2026-07-06 publication.

description: Will Nvidia's Rubin Ultra GPU reach first customer shipments in 2027, and in the reduced two-chiplet configuration — about half the performance of the originally planned four-die design that SemiAnalysis says was canceled on manufacturing-execution concerns — rather than the four-die version?
outcome: First customer shipments of Nvidia's Rubin Ultra GPU generation in 2027, and whether those chips use the two-chiplet design delivering roughly half the canceled four-die design's performance.
period: Calendar 2027 (the Rubin Ultra generation the item places around the 2027 launch, with Kyber racks housing Rubin Ultra originally slated for 2027). Checked against Nvidia's 2027 product/shipment disclosures and independent teardown/benchmark reports.

description: How large will the combined revenue of named merchant AI inference-chip startups (SambaNova and Rebellions) be in calendar 2026, and how fast is it growing relative to NVIDIA's data-center accelerator revenue?
outcome: SambaNova's and Rebellions' combined revenue for calendar 2026, as disclosed in their IPO filings or other public reports, versus NVIDIA's data-center revenue growth.
period: Calendar 2026 — checked against SambaNova's U.S. IPO prospectus/filings (considering a 2027 IPO) and Rebellions' Kospi IPO prospectus (planned Q1/Q2 2027), which would disclose 2026 revenue.
